2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the appellants as pre-emptors instituted Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No.44 of 1997 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Keranigonj, Dhaka stating, it alia, that the land covering 62 acres of CS Plot No.110 appertaining to CS Khatian No.36 originally belonged to Sheikh Karim Bepari and Sheikh Abdul Hamed Bepari. Sheikh Karim Bepari died leaving behind two sons named Abdul Aziz and Abdul Wahab. Thereafter, Abdul Aziz Bepari expired leaving behind three sons named Mohammad Hossen, Md. Mobarak Hossain (defendant No.2), Md. Habibullah (defendant No.3) and one daughter named Foyjunnessa. Mohammad Hossen passed away leaving behind the pre-emptors as his sons and two daughters, namely, Mst. Latifa. Begum and Mst. Shamsunnahar (opposite party Nos.4 and 5 of the application for preemption). The vendor (opposite party No.2 of the application for preemption) transferred the case land to the pre-emptee (opposite party No.1) by a kabala deed dated 16.06.1997. The pre-emptee is a stranger purchaser. The pre-emptor came to know about the impugned kabala deed on 12.11.1997 and then filed the application for pre-emption. 

 19. OPW1, Abeda Begum deposed that the case kabala giver, Md. Mobarak, is her paternal uncle who brought up her from her childhood and at one point of time, he left the homestead for another village named Baro Mahuria. She further deposed that since she was being brought up in the lap of her paternal uncle, he intended to gift his homestead to her and he donated this homestead 30 year back to her and since such gift, she has been living in the case premises on constructing house and filling earth. She further adds that she has got no other land excepting this only belonging and she would be driven in the street if she loses the case. She also adds that she mutated her name in case khatian soon after such oral gift and has been paying rent. This version of OPW 1 is corroborated by OPW2, Md. Mobarak Miah who deposed that Abeda is his brothel's daughter and she was brought up in his mess and he left the case homestead for Baro-Mahuria village and before leaving she gifted the case land to OPW1, Abeda Begum orally who has been living this homestead since such oral gift on erecting house therein. He further adds that present case kabala is nothing but an acknowledgment of such gift which has been donated 30 years back and this case kabala has been executed and register by him with a view to avoid further complicacy and for the purpose of creation of a registered instrument for the purposed of validating the earlier oral gift OPW3, Moslem Khan, OPW4, Tota Miah and OPW, Afil Miah are the close neighbor who categorically corroborated the fact of oral gift in favour of Abeda Begum. All the OPWs are aged persons. On perusal their testimonies, it appears that nothing cogent could be elicited to disbelieve those OPWs and as such, we have no hesitation to hold that the fact of oral gift has been done 30 years long before the case kabala. Thus, we find that the case kabala is nothing but a showing of transfer and cannot be considered as a sale deed within the meaning of section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act.
